# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Maya. Based in Portland, Oregon.
- Uses metric units by habit (Celsius, kilometres, grams) despite living in the US.

## Home and garden
- Avid vegetable gardener: heirloom tomatoes (Brandywine, Cherokee Purple), Genovese basil, runner
  beans, and a rhubarb crown that came from a neighbour.
- Four raised beds on the south side of the house, plus a cold frame built last spring.
- Keeps a compost bin going year-round; has strong opinions about coffee grounds and eggshells.
- Deals with aphids using ladybirds and a soap spray rather than anything systemic.
- Lost a whole crop of courgettes to powdery mildew two summers ago and still brings it up.

## Running
- Morning runner, 5-6 km most days before work, usually along the river path.
- Training for a spring half-marathon; current long run is 16 km.
- Went through three pairs of shoes last year and settled on a neutral trainer.

## Food and household
- Drinks green tea, mostly sencha; does not drink coffee.
- Vegetarian: no meat, but eats eggs and dairy.
- Bakes sourdough on weekends; the starter is named Bubbles and is about four years old.

## Family
- Two kids, ages 8 and 11, who both play soccer on weekends.
- Family camping trip to the Olympic Peninsula most Augusts.
- Learning ukulele, badly and cheerfully; likes folk and bluegrass.
profiles.raj:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Raj. Lives in Leeds, in a terraced house near a canal towpath.

## Cycling
- Commutes by bicycle year-round, about 9 km each way, on a steel touring frame bought secondhand.
- Does own maintenance: bottom brackets, wheel truing, cable replacement.
- Has ridden the Way of the Roses coast to coast twice, once in appalling weather.
- Keeps a spreadsheet of tyre pressures and puncture dates, which is treated as a joke by everyone
  except its author.

## Cooking
- Cooks South Indian food most weeknights; grinds dosa batter and ferments it overnight.
- Grows curry leaves in a pot that has to be dragged indoors every October.
- Owns three different sizes of tawa and considers this the minimum.
- Drinks filter coffee, made in a traditional steel filter, twice a day.

## Music and reading
- Plays tabla, about ten years in, practising most evenings for twenty minutes.
- Goes to a monthly jazz night above a pub; likes Alice Coltrane and Vijay Iyer.
- Reads mostly non-fiction: geology, canal history, Antarctic expeditions.

## Other
- Supports a lower-league football club and is stoic about it.
- One elderly greyhound, Sooty, who is walked twice a day regardless of weather.
- Learning Portuguese with an app, on a 400-day streak.
profiles.lena:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Lena. Lives in a small flat with a large balcony in Hamburg.

## Plants and birds
- Balcony herb garden: basil, mint, rosemary, thyme, and three chilli plants grown from seed.
- Keen birdwatcher; life list currently at 214 species, most recent addition a bluethroat.
- Weekend trips to the Wadden Sea coast in autumn for migrating waders.
- Owns a battered pair of 8x42 binoculars and a scope that is too heavy to carry far.

## Music
- Plays piano, intermediate level, currently working through the Chopin nocturnes.
- The flat has an upright piano that had to come in through a window.
- Goes to a community choir on Wednesdays, singing alto.

## Food and drink
- Pescatarian: eats fish, no other meat.
- Chamomile or peppermint tea in the evenings; an oat-milk latte in the morning.
- Makes an enormous batch of plum jam every September from a neighbour's tree.

## Home
- Two cats, Miso and Tofu, who are not allowed on the balcony unsupervised.
- Small pottery hobby: throws mugs and sells them at a local craft fair twice a year.
- Cycles everywhere; has never held a driving licence.
profiles.tomas:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Tomas. Lives outside Brno, Czech Republic, in a village of about 700 people.

## Mushrooms and the outdoors
- Serious mushroom forager; goes out most weekends from August to November.
- Can reliably distinguish the edible boletes from the bitter ones and enjoys explaining how.
- Dries and jars the surplus; the pantry holds about forty jars at any time.
- Cross-country skis in winter on tracks that start about a kilometre from the house.

## Woodwork
- Restores old furniture in a workshop in the barn, mostly interwar Czech pieces.
- Prefers hide glue and hand planes to anything powered, on the grounds that it is quieter.
- Currently rebuilding a bentwood chair with a broken back leg.

## Food
- Bakes rye bread every Sunday, from a starter kept in the cellar.
- Brews about 40 litres of beer a year, mostly a pale Czech lager that never quite comes out right.
- Eats meat but very little of it; most meals are potatoes, cabbage, and whatever is in the jars.

## Family and other
- Married, one daughter at university in Prague who visits monthly.
- Two beehives at the bottom of the garden; harvests roughly 25 kg of honey a year.
- Reads Czech and German fluently, and English well enough to be modest about it.
profiles.aisha:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Aisha. Lives in Manchester, in a flat above a bakery that is a mixed blessing.

## Climbing
- Boulders three evenings a week at a gym in an old railway arch.
- Currently projecting a V5 that has been unfinished for two months.
- Goes to the Peak District most fine weekends; prefers gritstone to limestone.
- Has strong views about chalk and does not use liquid chalk indoors.

## Languages and reading
- Speaks Arabic at home, English everywhere else, and is learning Japanese.
- Working through a graded reader series; about 900 kanji in.
- Reads a lot of translated fiction and keeps a notebook of sentences worth stealing.

## Food
- Cooks Levantine food most weekends; makes a batch of preserved lemons every winter.
- Does not drink alcohol; drinks a great deal of cardamom tea.
- Bakes maamoul at Eid using a wooden mould that belonged to a grandparent.

## Other
- Plays five-a-side football on Thursdays, in goal, under protest.
- One rescue cat, Nour, who is elderly and unimpressed by everything.
- Grew up in Bradford; visits family there roughly monthly on the train.
profiles.nils:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Nils. Lives in Bergen, Norway, on a steep street with 94 steps up to the door.

## Sailing
- Keeps a 28-foot wooden sailboat, built 1961, at a marina twenty minutes away.
- Spends most of April scraping, sanding and repainting the hull.
- Sails the fjords in summer, usually single-handed, occasionally as far as Sognefjord.
- Navigates on paper charts as well as electronics, out of habit rather than distrust.

## Weather and photography
- Follows the weather closely; can talk at length about föhn winds and orographic rain.
- Photographs coastline and boats, mostly on a 35mm film camera, and develops black and white
  film in the kitchen.
- Owns roughly 200 rolls of expired film bought at an estate sale.

## Food and drink
- Bakes skillingsboller most weekends and gives most of them away.
- Fishes for mackerel off the rocks in late summer; smokes some of the catch.
- Drinks filter coffee, strong, and a lot of it.

## Other
- Plays hardanger fiddle, poorly, having started at 41.
- Cross-country skis in winter; the season has been getting shorter and this is a sore subject.
- Two teenage sons, both taller than their parent, both indifferent to sailing.
profiles.priya:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Priya. Lives in Bengaluru, in a flat with a view of a rain tree.

## Textiles
- Weaves on a four-shaft floor loom that takes up most of the second bedroom.
- Works mostly in undyed cotton and khadi; recently started natural dyeing with indigo and madder.
- Takes an annual trip to Kutch to buy yarn and see block printers work.
- Has an unfinished shawl on the loom that has been unfinished since last Diwali.

## Birds and walking
- Walks in Cubbon Park most mornings before it gets hot.
- Keeps a garden bird list: coppersmith barbets, rose-ringed parakeets, and one memorable hoopoe.
- Goes to the Western Ghats in the monsoon, which everyone else considers the wrong season.

## Food
- Vegetarian, as most of the family is; cooks Tamil food and a lot of it.
- Makes filter coffee with chicory in a steel dabara every morning.
- Ferments idli batter twice a week and can tell the weather from how fast it rises.

## Other
- Reads Tamil poetry and English detective novels in roughly equal measure.
- Sings Carnatic music, learned as a child, resumed at 38 after a long gap.
- One large dog, Kumki, of no determinable breed.
profiles.diego:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Diego. Lives in Valparaíso, Chile, halfway up one of the hills.

## Football and running
- Plays in a Sunday league that has existed since before his involvement and will outlast it.
- Runs the stairs between cerros for training, which visitors find alarming.
- Watches lower-division Chilean football closely and top-flight European football casually.

## Astronomy
- Amateur astronomer; drives north to the Elqui valley two or three times a year.
- Owns an 8-inch Dobsonian telescope that barely fits in the car.
- Sketches what is seen at the eyepiece rather than photographing it; has about 60 sketches.
- Can find M83 without a chart and mentions this when the opportunity arises.

## Food
- Cooks a lot of seafood: congrio, machas, whatever the market has.
- Makes pebre from scratch and considers shop-bought an insult.
- Drinks maté in the afternoons, a habit picked up from an Argentine grandparent.

## Other
- Restores and repaints the metal railings on the stairs near the house, unpaid and unasked.
- Plays guitar, mostly nueva canción, and knows most of Violeta Parra by heart.
- One daughter, aged 6, who is learning to swim and is furious about it.
profiles.fiona:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Fiona. Lives on the Isle of Skye, in a croft house a mile from the road.

## Crofting and animals
- Keeps 30 blackface sheep and a small flock of hens.
- Lambing in April takes over everything; nothing else happens that month.
- Two working collies, Moss and Sula, who are not pets and are frequently treated as pets.
- Cuts and dries peat in early summer, which takes about a fortnight of good weather.

## Weather and sea
- Sea swims year-round, briefly in winter, from a beach twenty minutes' walk away.
- Watches the Atlantic weather come in and can usually call it a day ahead.
- Keeps a rain gauge and a handwritten weather log going back eleven years.

## Music and language
- Plays clàrsach, the small Scottish harp, and teaches two children in the village.
- Fluent Gaelic speaker; uses it at home and with neighbours.
- Goes to a fiddle session in Portree on the first Friday of the month.

## Food
- Bakes oatcakes weekly; makes bramble jelly every September.
- Eats a lot of lamb, unsurprisingly, and a lot of fish.
- Drinks tea constantly, strong, with milk.
profiles.kenji:
# MEMORY.md

## About this user
- Goes by Kenji. Lives in Kanazawa, Japan, near the old samurai district.

## Ceramics
- Studies Kutani-ware pottery on weekends with a teacher in her seventies.
- Throws on a kick wheel rather than an electric one, which takes twice as long.
- Fires in a shared gas kiln about six times a year; roughly a third of pieces survive.
- Collects chipped bowls from flea markets and repairs them with gold lacquer.

## Mountains
- Hikes in the Hakusan range from June to October, usually alone, always back before dark.
- Keeps a stamped hiking book with about 40 summit stamps in it.
- Owns snowshoes and uses them roughly once a year.

## Food
- Cooks a lot of fish and pickles vegetables in a wooden barrel in the entryway.
- Makes miso once a year in February with a group of neighbours.
- Drinks sencha in the morning and hojicha after dinner; almost never coffee.

## Other
- Practises shodo calligraphy on Tuesday evenings, about fifteen years in.
- Reads Edo-period travel diaries and modern nature writing.
- One indoor cat, Anko, named after sweet bean paste, who is the same colour.

maya:
## About this user
- Goes by Maya. Lives in Portland, Oregon, in a house with a south-facing back yard.
- Uses metric units by habit -- Celsius, kilometres, grams -- despite living in the US.
- Grew up in Michigan; moved west in her twenties and never went back.

## Garden
- Grows heirloom tomatoes (Brandywine, Cherokee Purple), Genovese basil and runner beans.
- Four raised beds along the south fence, plus a cold frame her neighbour helped her build.
- Keeps a compost bin going year-round and has strong opinions about coffee grounds.
- Lost a whole crop of courgettes to powdery mildew two summers ago and still brings it up.

## Running
- Runs 5 to 6 km most mornings before work, usually along the river path.
- Training for a spring half-marathon; her long run is up to 16 km.
- Went through three pairs of shoes last year before settling on a neutral trainer.
- Runs with a friend on Saturdays and alone the rest of the week.

## Food
- Drinks green tea, mostly sencha, and does not drink coffee.
- Vegetarian: no meat, though she eats eggs and dairy.
- Bakes sourdough at weekends; the starter is called Bubbles and is about four years old.
- Makes a large batch of tomato sauce every September and freezes most of it.

## Family
- Two children, aged 8 and 11, who both play soccer at weekends.
- The family camps on the Olympic Peninsula most Augusts, in the same spot each year.
- Her parents visit at Thanksgiving and stay a fortnight.
- Her brother lives in Chicago and they speak on the phone on Sundays.

## Music
- Learning ukulele, badly and cheerfully, about a year in.
- Likes folk and bluegrass; went to a festival in Oregon two summers running.
- Sings in the car and nowhere else.
- Her eldest is learning the trumpet, which the household is enduring.

## Outdoors
- Hikes in the Columbia River Gorge in spring, before the crowds arrive.
- Swims in the river in August when it is warm enough, which is not often.
- Can name most of the birds in her yard and is working on the warblers.
- Owns snowshoes she has used exactly twice.

## Around the house
- Two cats, Pepper and Fig, both elderly and both convinced it is dinner time.
- Repaints the porch railings every couple of summers, in the same green.
- Reads mostly novels in translation, a few a month, borrowed from the library.
- Plays cribbage with her neighbour on Thursday evenings.
raj:
## About this user
- Goes by Raj. Lives in Leeds, in a terraced house near a canal towpath.
- Born in Birmingham; his family is from Kerala and he visits every second winter.
- Walks to the market on Saturday mornings, rain or shine.

## Cycling
- Commutes by bicycle year-round, about 9 km each way, on a steel touring frame bought second-hand.
- Does his own maintenance: bottom brackets, wheel truing, cable replacement.
- Has ridden the Way of the Roses coast to coast twice, once in appalling weather.
- Fits winter tyres in November and takes them off some time in April, usually too late.

## Cooking
- Cooks South Indian food most weeknights and grinds his own dosa batter overnight.
- Grows curry leaves in a pot that has to come indoors every October.
- Owns three sizes of tawa and considers that the minimum.
- Makes a vat of sambar on Sundays that lasts most of the week.

## Music
- Plays tabla, about ten years in, practising most evenings for twenty minutes.
- Goes to a monthly jazz night above a pub near the station.
- Likes Alice Coltrane and Vijay Iyer, and is slowly coming round to free improvisation.
- His teacher is in her seventies and terrifying.

## Reading
- Reads mostly non-fiction: geology, canal history, Antarctic expeditions.
- Belongs to a reading group that meets in a pub and rarely discusses the book.
- Keeps a stack of half-finished books by the bed and feels guilty about it.
- Reads Malayalam slowly and is trying to get faster.

## Sport
- Supports a lower-league football club and is stoic about it.
- Plays badminton on Wednesdays in a draughty sports hall.
- Watches Test cricket in summer with the sound off and the radio on.
- Ran one half-marathon in 2019 and has no intention of repeating it.

## Dog
- One elderly greyhound, Sooty, walked twice a day regardless of weather.
- Sooty is afraid of the canal, of bicycles, and of the postman.
- Vet visits every six months for arthritis, which Raj takes seriously.
- The dog sleeps roughly twenty hours a day and Raj envies this openly.

## Languages
- Learning Portuguese, mostly from a phrasebook and a patient colleague.
- Speaks Malayalam at home with his parents and English everywhere else.
- Picked up enough Welsh on holidays to order breakfast.
- Enjoys etymology and will derail a conversation with it.
lena:
## About this user
- Goes by Lena. Lives in Hamburg, in a small flat with a large balcony.
- Grew up in Rostock; moved for work in her late twenties and stayed.
- Cycles everywhere and has never held a driving licence.

## Plants
- Balcony herb garden: basil, mint, rosemary, thyme and three chilli plants grown from seed.
- Overwinters the chillies indoors on a south windowsill with mixed success.
- Waters everything too much in spring and not enough in August.
- Trades cuttings with a neighbour two floors down.

## Birds
- Keen birdwatcher; her life list stands at 214 species, most recently a bluethroat.
- Takes weekend trips to the Wadden Sea coast in autumn for migrating waders.
- Owns a battered pair of 8x42 binoculars and a scope too heavy to carry far.
- Can identify most gulls by call, which she considers a mixed blessing.

## Piano
- Plays piano at intermediate level, currently working through the Chopin nocturnes.
- The flat has an upright piano that had to come in through a window.
- Practises for forty minutes most evenings, more at weekends.
- Accompanies a friend who sings, badly, once a month.

## Food
- Pescatarian: eats fish, no other meat.
- Chamomile or peppermint tea in the evenings; an oat-milk latte in the morning.
- Makes an enormous batch of plum jam every September from a neighbour's tree.
- Bakes a rye bread that takes two days and is worth it.

## Singing
- Sings alto in a community choir that meets on Wednesdays.
- The choir does two concerts a year and one disastrous summer picnic.
- She joined to meet people and stayed for the music.
- Sight-reads adequately and is quietly proud of it.

## Pottery
- Throws mugs on a wheel at a shared studio and sells them at a craft fair twice a year.
- Prefers stoneware to porcelain and matte glazes to gloss.
- About a third of what she makes survives the kiln, which she finds reasonable.
- Gives most of the rest away at Christmas.

## Cats
- Two cats, Miso and Tofu, not allowed on the balcony unsupervised.
- Miso is enormous and gentle; Tofu is small and a menace.
- Both were adopted from a shelter in Altona six years ago.
- The vet describes Miso's weight as "a project".
